Limerick and Clare Education and Training Board (ETB) is proud to be a key partner in the launch of Ireland’s first tertiary degree pathway into primary teaching, announced today in collaboration with Mary Immaculate College (MIC) and Tipperary Education and Training Board.

Limerick and Clare Education and Training Board (ETB) is proud to be a key partner in the launch of Ireland’s first tertiary degree pathway into primary teaching, announced today in collaboration with Mary Immaculate College (MIC) and Tipperary Education and Training Board.

It delivers educational services to over 49,000 students/learners across the region each year and has responsibility for 3 Community National Schools, 1 Community Special School, 17 Community Colleges, 28 College of Further Education and Training campuses, 1 Prison Education Centre, 2 Outdoor Education and Training Centres, and works with community groups in almost 300 locations across the region. Speaking about her experience at Croom Campus, Tara said “It was fantastic and very educational and I would recommend it for anyone who loves horses like me, my favourite part of the course was the hands-on experience working with horses in Clonshire.”

The pathway has been developed in close collaboration with the National Tertiary Office, aligning with national priorities to strengthen progression from further education into higher education and to support workforce needs in education.

Limerick and Clare ETB established one of six, national Local Creative Youth Partnerships (LCYPs) in 2019, under the auspices of Creative Ireland’s Creative Youth initiative. The Local Creative Youth Partnership Strategic Plan 2025-2027 aims to create more opportunities for young people to express themselves, support their educational journeys, and prioritise mental and emotional wellbeing.
